HOW TO RESTORE FROZEN-SPANNED   (SPANNED across 3 media)
==========================================================
This package's payload was byte-split across 3 tapes/drives as
FROZEN-SPANNED.seg001 … FROZEN-SPANNED.seg003. Every tape also carries this file
and FROZEN-SPANNED.manifest.json.gpg. The par2 set is on its OWN final tape (labelled ...-tape-4-of-4).

STEP 0 — GATHER and REJOIN.
Copy into ONE folder every tape's FROZEN-SPANNED.segNNN, and the par2 set
FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg.par2 and FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg.vol*.par2 (on its OWN final tape (labelled ...-tape-4-of-4)): par2
verify and repair in step 1 read them there. Then run ONE of:
     Windows:  copy /b FROZEN-SPANNED.seg001+FROZEN-SPANNED.seg002+FROZEN-SPANNED.seg003 FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg
     Unix/mac: cat FROZEN-SPANNED.seg* > FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg
(The zero-padded names sort into the correct order automatically.)

Now the normal restore, exactly as for a single-medium package:
1) VERIFY / REPAIR (no key needed):
     par2 verify FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg.par2
     par2 repair FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg.par2      (only if verify fails)
2) DECRYPT (prompts for the passphrase of key K-D0DF32B5):
     gpg -d -o FROZEN-SPANNED.tar FROZEN-SPANNED.tar.gpg
3) EXTRACT:
     tar -xf FROZEN-SPANNED.tar

Integrity (SHA256): payload e41f0ba2a471340c7bd27a9597f43c806ac6bf6bfe0e754b05f8fcd8ad518a53   tar 230c09c3b733df18cb789e82985fe422379bc2a30877f09cb64d8a4b8d908327
Custody chain: source file SHA-256s -> tar hash -> payload hash ->
per-segment hashes (manifest / catalog) link every tape to the originals.
Full file list: FROZEN-SPANNED.manifest.json.gpg (encrypted; see PRIVACY below)
No compression anywhere — extracted bytes are the originals.
==========================================================

WINDOWS — the tar built into Windows writes each file name in the system's
code page. A name that code page cannot hold (Japanese on a Western system,
for example) is refused with "unreadable filename", and the other files are
restored. The package keeps every name as UTF-8: to restore those files too,
extract FROZEN-SPANNED.tar with a tar that keeps Unicode names, such as 7-Zip
(7z x FROZEN-SPANNED.tar).

PRIVACY — this medium's file listing is ENCRYPTED (FROZEN-SPANNED.manifest.json.gpg),
so a lost tape reveals no filenames. To read it:
     gpg -d FROZEN-SPANNED.manifest.json.gpg      (passphrase for key K-D0DF32B5)
